Theme 089 · Art movements & eras

Pop-Art Ben-Day

1960s Pop Art in the Lichtenstein manner: comic panels, thick ink outlines, hand-screened Ben-Day dots, caption boxes and speech balloons. The anomaly becomes an onomatopoeia — ZAP! — and the hero of the story is the Acme mark, which gets its own splash-panel entrance.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Comic panel — thick 10 px ink border around a Ben-Day dot field
  • Ben-Day dots — SVG pattern of offset circles in tinted teal, amber or coral
  • Speech balloon — ellipse + tail; the Acme mark 'speaks' the alert
  • Caption box — amber rectangle with narration ("Friday, 5:58 PM…")
  • Onomatopoeia burst — spiky star with stroked lettering — PULSE!, ZAP!
  • Comic button — coral pill with hard 10 px ink drop shadow, skewed −6°

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Panel pop — scale 1.15→1 and rotate 2°→0, back.out(2) 0.25 s, one panel per beat
  • Burst bang — scale 0→1.1→1 over 0.3 s + ±8 px shake for 4 frames, exactly on the drop and on the anomaly
  • Dot breathe — Ben-Day radius 5→6.5→5 px, sine.inOut 0.5 s per beat — the page throbs with the kick

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Comics are the fastest narrative format there is: panels, balloons and captions tell a before/after story with no voice-over, and ZAP! makes the anomaly fun rather than scary. Risk: it can feel juvenile or cheap; keep the data accurate, the outlines consistent and the jokes minimal.

Adapt to your product: Script your product's key moment as three panels — problem, product speaks, human acts — and let your logo be the character with the speech balloon. Your UI can appear on in-panel monitors.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben-Day_dots — the printing dot technique and its use in Pop Art · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Lichtenstein — Lichtenstein: Whaam!, bold outlines, flat colour, Ben-Day dots
